name: CathBot
group: Imperial College London, Hamlyn Centre (Dagnino, Kundrat, Yang)
versions: 2018 haptic active constraints (Dagnino IROS); 2021 MR-safe platform (Kundrat TBME); 2023 in-vivo platform (Dagnino TBME)
target_anatomy: renal, mesenteric, iliac and carotid arteries (pig); thoracic/abdominal phantoms
devices_driven: one catheter and one guidewire, one at a time (not simultaneously); standard instruments, plug-and-play carriers
n_dof_detail: 6 per Kundrat Sec. II-C (three actuated axes per instrument); 4 per LegoBot Table I
translation_detail: clamp-relay (pneumatic clamps with pneumatic stepper drivers, regripping; single stroke 20 mm per review Table IV)
rotation_detail: pneumatic rotary stepper (0.3 mm and 10 deg steps)
device_range: N.R. (supplement not opened); 6 Fr sheath in the pig study
force_sensing: none on follower; haptics rendered from image-derived tip-to-wall distance
haptics_leader: yes: handle with linear and rotary motors renders viscous force/torque; virtual fixtures slow the follower near the wall
imaging_compat: MR-Safe (ASTM F2503 class); used under fluoroscopy
validation_detail: 4 pigs, 5 target arteries, cannulation and balloon angioplasty, robot vs manual; earlier phantom user study with 7 vascular surgeons/registrars
key_numbers: success 100% both; completion 35+-14 min robot vs 15+-6 min manual (p=0.03); fluoroscopy 7+-5 vs 2+-1 min; feed 7-10 mm/s, max 30 mm/s; actuator latency 10-15 ms; clamp holding force 10.2 N (calc.)
sim_model: none found for the robot (Kundrat/Dagnino texts)
sim2real_detail: none found (Hamlyn learning-from-demonstration studies listed by search, e.g. Chi ICRA 2020, were not matched to CathBot hardware)
